_request.system:
You classify a single ERP requirement into exactly one of four delivery tiers, using only the SAP standard-process knowledge entries provided to you.

  Fit           The delivered standard already does this once baseline org structures exist.
  Configuration The delivered logic does this, driven by values maintained in customizing                 (thresholds, code lists, org units, number ranges, determination rules). No code.
  Enhancement   The standard process still drives the flow, but a delivered object must carry an                 extra custom field, or extra logic must run at a published extension point.
  Development   The standard provides no object, no process, and no extension point covering the                 request; a new program, interface, or persistence must be built and maintained.

Method:
- Reason from the knowledge entries' stated boundaries: what the standard covers, what is a   configuration point, and what is stated to be beyond the standard.
- Do NOT classify from surface features. "It mentions an external system" is not a reason.   The reason must be that the standard provides no object, process, or extension point for it,   and that the transport, mapping, scheduling, and error handling are project deliverables.
- A requirement to make an already-delivered field required is field-status configuration.   A requirement to enforce entry in a field the delivered object does not have, or to gate a   process on a condition the standard data model does not carry, is an enhancement.
- In rationale, cite the specific entry IDs whose boundary decided the call, and say what that   boundary is. Cite only entries you were given.
- Set confidence below 0.7 when the entries conflict or none of them squarely covers the request.
_request.user:
Requirement (master_data): An upload from the SeltraBridge archive must bring over product drawings and link them to product records.

Verbatim from the workshop: "an upload from the fictional SeltraBridge archive that brings over product drawings and links them to product records"

Knowledge entries retrieved for this requirement:

### KB-MD-008 — Documents, drawings, and attachments on master records [master_data]
Standard process: The delivered attachment service lets users attach files and links to master records, and the document management content models controlled documents with document types, statuses, versions, and object links that bind a document to a product or a partner. Attaching a drawing to a product by hand is delivered behaviour. Moving a large body of drawings out of an external archive, deciding from the archive's metadata which product each drawing belongs to, and creating the object links in bulk is a build: the reading of the archive, the matching rule, the error handling for unmatched files, and the rerun behaviour are all project deliverables.
Capabilities covered by the standard: Attachment service for files and links on business objects.; Document info records with types, versions, statuses, and originals.; Object links binding documents to products, partners, and documents.; Authorization and status-driven access to originals.
Common configuration points: Document types, number ranges, and status networks.; Object link definitions and the storage categories for originals.
Typically beyond the standard: Bulk extraction of originals from an external archive with project-defined matching rules.; Recurring synchronization between an outside document repository and the ERP system.

### KB-P2P-004 — Sourcing, contracts, and info records [P2P]
Standard process: The delivered sourcing content determines where a requisition is sourced from. Purchasing info records hold the supplier-material relationship and its conditions, outline agreements hold negotiated terms and release quantities, and the source list can restrict or fix which supplier may be used for a material at a plant. Quota arrangements distribute demand across several suppliers by percentage. Source determination during requisition and order creation reads this content and proposes or fixes the supplier. All of it is master data and customizing; none of it requires code.
Capabilities covered by the standard: Purchasing info records with price conditions and planned delivery time.; Outline agreements including quantity and value contracts and scheduling agreements.; Source list and quota arrangement driven source determination.; Automatic supplier proposal during requisition conversion.
Common configuration points: Whether a source list is mandatory for a plant.; Condition types and pricing procedures used in purchasing.; Document types for outline agreements.
Typically beyond the standard: Source determination driven by a score or rating maintained outside the ERP system.; Sourcing rules that cannot be expressed as source list, quota, or contract content.

### KB-MD-004 — Product master standard views [master_data]
Standard process: The product master is organized as a set of views layered over organizational levels. Client-level data carries the product number, product type, base unit of measure, product group, weights, and dimensions. Plant-level views carry planning, procurement, and quality attributes. Valuation views carry the price control indicator, the valuation class, and the standard or moving average price. Sales and storage views carry the remaining organizational attributes. Creating a product with product type, base unit, product group, plant views, and valuation views is delivered behaviour and requires only that the organizational levels exist.
Capabilities covered by the standard: Client-level attributes including product type, base unit, product group, and old product number.; Plant-level views for planning, procurement, and quality management.; Valuation views with price control, valuation class, and price.; Language-dependent product descriptions and alternative units of measure.
Common configuration points: Product types and the views they permit.; Number ranges per product type, internal or external.; Field selection per product type, plant, and transaction.; Valuation classes and their account determination.
Typically beyond the standard: Attributes that no delivered view carries, such as project-specific handling classifications.; Attaching externally sourced documents to products in bulk according to a project's linkage rules.

### KB-XC-002 — Integration with non-SAP, legacy, and third-party systems [cross_cutting]
Standard process: The ERP publishes released APIs and message interfaces for its business objects, and these are part of the delivered standard. What the standard does not deliver is the interface itself. A project-specific connection to a named external application always has to be built: somebody must design the payload mapping, decide the trigger and schedule, implement error handling and retry, provide monitoring and reprocessing, and own the interface for its lifetime. This remains true even when both endpoints are entirely standard and even when the data being moved is standard data. Recurring extracts, nightly file drops, spreadsheet imports, portal order intake, and pushes into an external ledger or archive all share this property: the transport, the mapping, and the operational surface are project deliverables, not shipped content.
Capabilities covered by the standard: Released OData and A2X services for reading and writing master data and documents.; Message-based interfaces for common document exchange patterns.; Standard inbound processing for widely adopted electronic document formats.; Application logs and monitoring for delivered interface frameworks.
Common configuration points: Communication arrangements, partner profiles, and endpoint destinations.; Message types and their assignment to partners.; Output determination that decides when a document triggers an outbound message.
Typically beyond the standard: Any bespoke interface to a specifically named external or legacy application.; Scheduled extracts whose file layout is defined by the receiving system.; Converting an external portal's payload into ERP documents when the payload is not a standard format.; Importing values maintained in an external spreadsheet or archive into ERP records.

parsed.rationale: The requirement is for an upload from an external archive (SeltraBridge) to bring product drawings and link them to products in bulk. According to KB-MD-008, the standard delivers attachment service and document management with object links, but 'Moving a large body of drawings out of an external archive, deciding from the archive's metadata which product each drawing belongs to, and creating the object links in bulk is a build: the reading of the archive, the matching rule, the error handling for unmatched files, and the rerun behaviour are all project deliverables.' KB-MD-004 also states that attaching externally sourced documents to products in bulk according to project linkage rules is beyond the standard. Furthermore, KB-XC-002 confirms that a project-specific connection to a named external application is a build. Therefore, the requirement falls into Development because the standard provides no pre-built interface for this specific archive extraction and bulk linking with project-defined matching.
